About Chalong

Chalong lies inland of Chalong Bay, between Rawai, Kata and Phuket Town, around the Chalong roundabout. It is mainly residential, with housing estates, villas with gardens, condominiums and local businesses.

The bay itself is a working harbour with Chalong Pier rather than a swimming beach; residents drive to Rawai, Nai Harn or Kata for the beach.

Our catalogue lists both condominiums near the Chalong roundabout and Wat Chalong and new pool-villa estates on the quieter Palai side towards Chalong Bay.

Why buyers choose Chalong

  • Wat Chalong and the Big Buddha viewpoint nearby
  • Chalong Pier for boat and dive trips
  • Large supermarkets, gyms and Muay Thai camps
  • Central for Rawai, Kata and Phuket Town

Neighbouring areas in our catalogue: Rawai · Nai Harn · Kata · Phuket Town

Lifestyle and amenities

Chalong has big supermarkets, international and local restaurants, gyms and some of Phuket's best-known Muay Thai camps. It is practical for everyday life and less touristy than the beach towns, with quick access to the south-coast beaches and Phuket Town.

Beaches and surroundings

Chalong Bay is used by boats and the pier, so it is not a swimming beach. Rawai, Nai Harn and Kata beaches are typically 10 to 20 minutes away by car.

Rental demand in Chalong

Chalong is a long-term rental market. Demand comes from families, long-stay residents, people working in the south of the island and those training at fitness and Muay Thai camps. Holiday demand is limited because there is no swimming beach.

Long-term rentals

Houses and villas with gardens are popular with families; condos with people training or working locally.

Short-term rentals

Mostly fitness and Muay Thai visitors on monthly stays; little classic beach-holiday demand.

Suitable property types

Houses and pool villas with gardens; practical condos.

Advantages and limitations

Advantage: value for money and a central location. Limitations: no swimming beach and traffic around the Chalong roundabout.

General market observations, not verified statistics. No rental income or occupancy is guaranteed; developer-advertised returns are not market results.

Rental and investment in Chalong

Chalong attracts buyers looking for value and long-term rental demand rather than beach-front holiday letting. Houses and villas on quieter side roads suit family tenants.

Typical investor profiles

Owner-occupiers and long-term rental buyers.

Risks to consider

Lower holiday demand; many similar housing estates compete for tenants.

Ownership costs

Maintenance, garden and pool care, insurance and periods between tenants.

Chalong: frequently asked questions

Is there a beach in Chalong?

Chalong Bay is used by boats and the pier and is not a swimming beach. Rawai, Nai Harn and Kata beaches are about 10 to 20 minutes away by car.

Is Chalong a good place to live in Phuket?

Chalong suits people who want a practical, central base with supermarkets, gyms and schools nearby, and good value compared with the beach areas.

What is Chalong Pier used for?

Chalong Pier is the main departure point for boat and dive trips to the islands south of Phuket.

Can I buy property in Chalong?

Yes. Our catalogue lists new condominiums such as Wyndham Fantasea Condo Chalong and Andaman Bay View Residences, and villa estates such as Botanica Chalong Bay, 9 Nile Residence and Unique Eco Viva. Foreigners can buy condo units freehold within the foreign quota; villas are usually bought on a registered lease.

Is Chalong good for families?

Yes, many families choose Chalong for houses with gardens at lower prices than the beach areas, with schools and shops nearby.

How much does property in Chalong cost?

Advertised starting prices for projects in Chalong run from ฿2,636,000 to ฿37,639,000 (5 of 5 projects publish a price). These are lowest advertised prices; ask us to confirm current availability.
